The retrieved documents describe multiple events in the surrender timeline: the offer to surrender (d3: August 10), the announcement of surrender (d4, d8: August 14; d1, d6: August 15), and the formal signing ceremony (d1, d5, d6, d9: September 2). These are complementary stages of a single process, not conflicting facts.

The evidence collectively details the sequence from Japan's initial offer to the final formal ceremony. d1, d6, and d9 explicitly state the formal signing occurred on September 2, 1945, while d4 and d8 note President Truman's announcement on August 14, and d3 covers the initial offer on August 10. These are all correct parts of the historical timeline.

The Japanese surrender involved a sequence of events. Japan offered to surrender on August 10, 1945 [d3]. The surrender was announced by President Truman on August 14 and by Emperor Hirohito on August 15, 1945 [d4][d1][d6]. The formal surrender ceremony, which officially ended World War II, took place aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945 [d1][d5][d9].
